summary: Defines a number of additional link relation types that can be used for various purposes in a variety of application types. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Adds more name tags to describe how one web thing is related to another, like next page or help page.

subtitle: Five new names for describing how web resources relate to each other.

tldr.problem: Web pages and APIs need to express relationships between resources (a page about a product, a preview version of a video, a privacy policy), but only a few link relation types were registered.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC adds five new link relation types to the Web Linking registry: about, preview, privacy-policy, terms-of-service, and type. These can appear in HTTP Link headers or in HTML link tags to describe the relationship between the current resource and a target resource.
tldr.outcome: Web applications and servers can now clearly indicate where privacy policies, terms of service, previews, and semantic types are found. The Link header becomes more expressive for metadata and navigation.

today: RFC 6903 is an Informational RFC published in March 2013 and has not been obsoleted. The five link relations are now standard and widely used by web services and APIs to indicate privacy policies, terms of service, previews, and semantic types.

sections.title: What Are Link Relations
sections.content:
Web Linking is the standard way to describe a relationship between two web resources. A resource can include a Link header or HTML <link> tags to point to a related resource and give the relationship a name. RFC 5988 established the framework; this RFC adds five new names to the registry.

Link relations are useful for navigation (next, previous, up), authentication (openid2.provider), and metadata (canonical, alternate). They let servers tell clients about related resources without embedding them in the content.
sections.eli5: A web link is just an arrow from one page to another with a label saying what the relationship is. Like "this is the next page" or "here is the privacy policy". This RFC adds five new label types.

sections.title: The Five New Link Relations
sections.content:
The about relation indicates that the target resource is the subject or topic of the context. If you are reading a product review, the about link points to the product being reviewed. Multiple about links can reference multiple subjects.

The preview relation points to a preview version of the context: a low-quality or shortened version, a thumbnail, a screen capture, or a snippet. A video server might return a link to a 10-second preview when you request the full video.

The privacy-policy relation points to the privacy policy describing how personal information is collected, stored, and used. A website can include this link in the page header or HTTP Link header. The RFC warns that the presence of a privacy-policy link does not create a legal obligation unless there is an explicit contract.

The terms-of-service relation points to the terms under which the service is offered. Like privacy policy, the presence of a terms-of-service link is a notice of expected rules, not a binding contract unless formally agreed.
sections.eli5: "About" tells you what a page is discussing. "Preview" shows you a smaller version before you download. "Privacy policy" and "terms of service" are legal documents that sites link to, so visitors know the rules.

sections.title: Semantic Types and Other Uses
sections.content:
The type relation indicates the semantic type or category of the context resource. Unlike the HTTP Content-Type header, which describes the serialization format (JSON, HTML, plain text), the type link describes the abstract kind of thing being represented.

For example, a plain-text response could include a type link to http://example.org/Person to indicate the response represents a person, even though it is transmitted as plain text. Multiple type links can indicate multiple semantic types for the same resource.
sections.eli5: Content-Type tells you the file format (HTML, JSON, plain text). The type link tells you what kind of thing the page is describing (a person, a product, an event). They are different ideas.

sections.title: Registration in IANA
sections.content: All five relation types have been registered in the IANA Link Relation Types registry, making them standard names that any web application or server can use. The registry is maintained by IANA and published online, so any specification can reference these relations by name.
sections.eli5: The IANA registry is like a phone book for link names. Once a name is registered, any website can use it and everyone knows what it means.
